entries.title: SPINET: Sheaf Protein Inverse Folding Network
entries.abstract_excerpt: Proteins change shape as they function, yet most inverse folding models predict amino acid sequences from a single, fixed backbone. A central challenge in protein engineering is to design proteins that undergo specific motions, which requires accounting for how their structures change over time. This motivates inverse protein folding conditioned on protein motion. We introduce SPINET, which predicts sequences from molecular dynamics trajectories. It uses cellular sheaves to represent residue interactions within each frame and recurrent units to integrate information across frames, then predicts all amino acids in a single pass.
